{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABZes4Tg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhDF6fM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 37, "title": "Implement clocked SH-2 B-bus memory read transactions", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

At `bfe51271b33f75821258a250d665fcdaf6f90f29`, `CpuBus::external_read_group` chooses `min(BSC width, operand width)` and submits those reads directly. `complete_bus_transaction` can consequently sample four B-bus memory bytes together. This does not implement the SCU bridge's documented read-unit conversion and separately completed downstream transfers.

The distinction matters when CPUs read video or sound memory while hardware accesses that memory: correct final bytes alone do not establish correct acquisition, contention or completion ordering. Existing SCU DMA halfword tests exercise a different bus-master path.

## Expected outcome

Implement scheduled SH-2 reads through the SCU B-bus **memory** bridge for both processors. Separate the architectural operand, CPU-facing transaction and downstream B-bus phases. Retain sampled data across waits and interpreter replay, apply the appropriate target's arbitration to each physical phase, and extract the requested operand lanes according to the documented bridge contract.

Primary references:

- [SCU Final Specifications, ST-210](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-210-110194.pdf), §3 item 32, printed p.9: narrow CPU reads in the A/B-bus region involve longword external accesses; writes retain their access size.
- [SCU User's Manual, ST-097-R5](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-097-R5-072694.pdf), §2.1 and §3.2, including figs.3.6–3.8: bus interfaces and physical transfer sequencing.
- [SCSP User's Manual, ST-077-R2](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-077-R2-052594.pdf), §§3.1–3.2, printed pp.18–21 and fig.3.2: interface widths and sound-memory ownership.
- [VDP2 User's Manual](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p03_31.htm), §3.3: VRAM access allocation.

Focus on sound RAM, VDP1 VRAM/draw framebuffer, and VDP2 VRAM/CRAM, including their existing aliases. Preserve architectural alignment, sign extension, cache behavior and memory geometry.

This task does not extend the conversion speculatively to side-effecting MMIO. In particular, item 32 alone does not establish extra CD FIFO pops, adjacent register reads or interrupt acknowledgements. The [CD communication manual, ST-162](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-162-062094.pdf), §3.1/table3.1, separately specifies communication-register access widths. Keep MMIO, A-bus conversion and CPU writes explicitly outside this increment, with their remaining contracts recorded.

## Context and reproduction

Inspection baseline: `bfe51271b33f75821258a250d665fcdaf6f90f29`.

- `src/bus.rs:1234`: CPU external reads retain operand-sized requests without a distinct SCU memory-bridge unit.
- `src/bus/transactions.rs:1194`: a four-byte CPU request can reach `Bus::read::<4>` at one completion.
- `src/bus/transactions.rs:907`: SCU DMA already selects downstream widths and retains partial units separately.
- `src/bus/transactions.rs:1775`: the existing SCU DMA test demonstrates independently sampled B-bus halfwords, but does not cover CPU reads.
- `src/bus/vram_grant_tests.rs` and `src/bus/sound_tests.rs` provide existing target-contention regressions to extend.

Reproduce the CPU defect with scheduled reads whose backing halfwords change between independently specified physical completion boundaries. Add narrow-read occupancy checks that distinguish operand-sized acquisition from the documented bridge unit. These tests must fail against the inherited CPU path.

The supplied snapshot reports no open task Issues. Main CI was observed in progress; that is neither failure nor successful validation. This planning pass used read-only inspection and primary references, without rerunning complete acceptance suites.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document a primary-derived transaction table covering operand widths, alignment, lane extraction, downstream phase order, completion, and the distinction between CPU-side and B-bus observations. Identify supported accesses and software-prohibited cases, including SCSP main-interface byte restrictions. Cite applicable corrections and distinguish specified timing from deterministic model conventions.
- [ ] Implement the scoped bridge reads in production execution for both SH-2s. Each physical phase must acquire its target, sample at its completion, and retain its result through waits/replay. A whole longword must not be sampled through one backing-memory read. Complete the architectural operand at the boundary established by the documented contract.
- [ ] Add independent native vectors for every scoped memory endpoint, both processors, all valid byte/word lanes and longword reads, existing mirrors/P1 aliases, cache hits and refills. Use literal expected bytes and manually derived event sequences rather than production timing helpers as the oracle.
- [ ] Demonstrate retained first-halfword data and separately sampled second-halfword data using before/at/after completion mutations. Verify narrow-read bridge occupancy independently of returned values. Include actual failing negative controls against the inherited atomic and operand-sized paths.
- [ ] Exercise relevant VDP2 display grants, VDP1 local-memory ownership, SCSP PCM/DSP/DMA/refresh contention, and competing CPU/SCU requests. Verify no early architectural result, repeated completed access or unintended starvation. Results and event order must agree across advancement chunks 1/3/17/10000 and intervening debugger inspection.
- [ ] Test reset during queued and partially completed reads on both processors, respecting the existing documented power/manual reset domains. No stale journal result may enter a restarted CPU. Preserve alignment exceptions, bounded failure handling and the existing cache/coherence contract.
- [ ] Add an original, explicitly MIT-licensed guest fixture that initializes its own data, executes reads on both SH-2s, measures relevant timing with guest FRT instructions, and records computed results in ordinary RAM. Exercise sound and video memory, repeated cold boots, changed source operands and an omitted/replaced-read control. Reproduce source, bytes and authored golden records in CI.
- [ ] Execute the identical fixture through native Machine execution and rebuilt production Wasm in headless Chromium under `/saturn-rust/`. Compare guest-computed records with independent expectations; host code must not supply results or replace guest reads.
- [ ] Preserve all existing tests and Star Collector, Prism Courier and Hardware Lab behavior. Any changed historical timing expectation must have an exact primary reference and rationale; retain its original regression purpose. Confirm MMIO FIFO/clear-on-read behavior and CPU write strobes have not changed incidentally.
- [ ] Update `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/hardware-conformance.md` and a focused validation record with implementation/test links, actual negative-control results and remaining deviations. Evidence-backed corrections to this AI-authored contract may be documented autonomously; do not weaken validation to accommodate failures or introduce human-confirmation gates.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native all-target and Wasm Clippy with warnings denied, registered fixture/media reproduction checks, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, and the complete extended `npm run test:browser`, without required skips.

This is a partial #17 increment. Remaining CPU/peripheral semantics, board arbitration/reset, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and comprehensive integration requirements remain mandatory. Keep #17's unmet scope explicit and use no umbrella closing keywords. Commercial-game compatibility remains unverified without lawful compatibility testing.

## Optional validation

Additional generated read/contention schedules checked against an independent reference model. No personal firmware, commercial media or physical console is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
